title: Project Proposal
content:
VIETNAM IT JOB MARKET IT recruitment data collection, processing and analytics on AWS 1. Executive summary Vietnam IT Job Market collects ITviec listings with Python, processes JSON on one EC2 and publishes analytical Parquet to S3. Glue Data Catalog provides metadata for Athena. Streamlit and Plotly deliver analytics through Nginx HTTPS. The deployment region is ap-southeast-1. Personal data is stored in S3; moderation state and audit are stored in DynamoDB.
2. Problem statement Individual listings are difficult to aggregate manually and repeated collection requires deduplication, validation and change tracking. Users need saved jobs and self-managed application tracking; administrators need reversible moderation and traceable operations. The dataset covers accessible ITviec listings, not the entire Vietnamese IT labour market. No measured financial ROI is claimed.
3. Solution architecture The recruitment flow is ITviec → EC2 Python → raw/current/history/clean JSON → S3 Parquet → Athena with Glue metadata → Streamlit/Plotly. Run artifacts remain separate from the canonical analytics prefix. Accounts and personal activity use S3 objects. DynamoDB moderation transactions write state and audit; a Projection Worker publishes an S3 snapshot for Athena filtering. The application also checks DynamoDB. These services do not form one atomic transaction.
One EC2 simplifies the project deployment but is a shared failure point. Glue is used as Data Catalog, while Python on EC2 performs ETL.
4. Technical implementation Discovery and batches are validated before ETL; collectors process up to 25 URLs per batch by default. Current records use job_id, retain first_seen and update last_seen. Missing listings alone do not imply expiry. Cleaning and Parquet export are checked for schema and row-count consistency. ETag conditions, staging, journals and backups support controlled publication.
Guest users explore public analytics. USER adds saved jobs, application tracking, profile and password management. ADMIN adds six administration pages, for ten pages overall. The dashboard has four overall and four weekly KPIs plus seven chart groups. Weekly comparisons use retained listings by posting date; application tracking does not submit CVs.
Deployment records describe t3.small Ubuntu 24.04 with encrypted 30 GiB gp3 storage. Streamlit runs as vnjob on 127.0.0.1:8501; Nginx exposes HTTPS and forwards WebSocket traffic. Runtime uses an IAM Role and IMDSv2. Passwords use salted PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 with 600,000 iterations. Role, account status and session checks protect actions.
systemd schedules the pipeline daily at 02:00 Vietnam time. Projection runs every two minutes. The Operations Worker validates allowlisted administrator recovery requests. Certbot and an IP-aware helper maintain HTTPS; CloudWatch records logs and pipeline failures. Email notifications are not established by the presence of a Console alarm.
5. Implementation roadmap Phase Deliverable Design Source scope, schema, roles and architecture Collection and ETL Validated artifacts, current/history, cleaned JSON and Parquet Analytics Canonical S3 data, Glue metadata and Athena views Application Dashboard, personal features and moderation Deployment EC2 services, HTTPS, timers, workers and monitoring Acceptance Dated tests, screenshots, runbook and Workshop Phases do not assert dates that are absent from project records. The twelve-week learning log is separate.
6. Budget basis Costs comprise EC2 runtime/credits, EBS, public IPv4, S3 storage/requests, Athena scans, DynamoDB, CloudWatch and applicable transfer. Actual Billing data or a documented estimate is required before publishing a monthly total. Parquet, caching, a single canonical analytics file and log retention provide cost controls; no savings percentage or complete Free Tier coverage is claimed.
7. Risk assessment Source changes and blocking can interrupt collection; validation and bounded retry do not guarantee coverage. Schema or duplicate files can distort analysis. Publication journals and conditional writes support recovery, while moderation projection remains eventually consistent. A single EC2, changing public IPs and certificate dependencies can interrupt access. Runtime roles, private configuration and server-side session checks reduce access risks. Backup verification is separate from production restoration across all data stores.
8. Expected outcomes and recorded evidence Expected deliverables are validated recruitment processing, usable analytics, persistent personal features, auditable moderation and observable operation.
The 02 November deployment report records 140 unit tests, six UI smoke suites, 130 matching file checksums, eight KPIs, one jobs table and ten ADMIN pages. HTTP redirected with 301; HTTPS/health returned 200; TLS and WebSocket checks passed. The 03 November HTTPS report records timer and certificate checks but no completed stop/start drill. These are dated records, not current live AWS verification. No large-scale load capacity or financial ROI is established.
The Vietnamese proposal contains the full submission text, detailed risk/cost tables and exact positions for five real-image groups.

title: Self-Assessment
content:
I am Vu Thi Phuc, a student of class CNTTB, majoring in Information Technology at the Vietnam National University of Agriculture, participating in the First Cloud AI Journey internship program at AWS Vietnam.
The goal of this internship is to strengthen my foundational knowledge, become familiar with AWS services, and apply what I have learned to the Vietnam IT Job Market project. Over the 12-week internship, the main topics studied through Cloud Journey were documented in my worklog and connected to each stage of collecting, processing, storing, querying, and visualizing recruitment data from ITviec.
The learning process and project implementation have provided opportunities to improve my skills in researching documentation, reviewing configurations, identifying the causes of errors, and presenting results based on verified information. The table below summarizes my self-assessment across different criteria.
No. Criteria Description Good Fair Average 1 Professional Knowledge and Skills Have a basic understanding of AWS and the roles of Python, EC2, S3, Glue Data Catalog, Athena, DynamoDB, and CloudWatch in the project. □ ☑ □ 2 Learning Ability Able to research documentation and complete exercises step by step. Need more time to review and apply new knowledge. □ ☑ □ 3 Initiative Independently explore project components, review source code, and check steps that may cause errors. ☑ □ □ 4 Sense of Responsibility Monitor assigned tasks, verify results, and review data before including it in reports. ☑ □ □ 5 Discipline Follow the work plan, complete practical exercises according to instructions, and protect sensitive configuration information. ☑ □ □ 6 Willingness to Improve Listen to feedback, explore unclear topics, and make necessary adjustments. ☑ □ □ 7 Communication Present ideas clearly, describe encountered problems specifically, and share results so others can easily follow. ☑ □ □ 8 Teamwork Actively communicate, listen to others’ opinions, and cooperate with team members when support is needed. ☑ □ □ 9 Professional Conduct Respect mentors, team members, and shared working regulations. ☑ □ □ 10 Problem-Solving Skills Investigate issues related to access permissions, data, queries, or services and examine logs before drawing conclusions. □ ☑ □ 11 Contribution to the Project/Organization Participate in project implementation, summarize documentation, and add practical instructions to support project handover. ☑ □ □ 12 Overall Performance Complete basic learning activities, participate in project implementation, and identify skills that require further improvement. □ ☑ □ Strengths During the Internship Applying AWS Knowledge to the Project: Understand how Python on EC2 processes data, Amazon S3 stores Parquet files, and AWS Glue Data Catalog provides table metadata for queries using Amazon Athena. Understanding How System Components Work Together: Understand that account data and personal activity information are stored in S3, while moderation information and audit logs are stored in DynamoDB. Recognize the role of the Projection Worker in data synchronization. Verifying Information Before Reporting: Review source code, configurations, commands, and test results to determine the verification status of each function deployed on AWS. Organizing Documentation Step by Step: Structure worklogs, proposals, and workshop materials so readers can follow each stage and compare the results. Areas for Improvement Strengthening Technical Knowledge: Practice optimizing Athena queries, configuring appropriate IAM permissions, and evaluating operational costs based on actual usage data. Improving Troubleshooting and Recovery Skills: Develop skills in analyzing logs, handling data pipeline interruptions, checking backups, and practicing recovery scenarios involving EC2 restarts. Writing Clearer and More Concise Technical Documentation: Use diagrams, actual screenshots, test dates, or execution IDs to help readers verify and reproduce results. Enhancing Testing Skills: Practice designing integration test scenarios, measuring system performance, and clearly documenting whether tests were performed locally or on AWS. Tracking Progress More Consistently: Divide tasks into smaller steps and update worklogs regularly to identify difficulties and unresolved issues earlier. Future Development After the Internship After completing the internship, I plan to continue studying Python, Data Engineering, and Cloud Computing, while strengthening my skills in data processing, SQL querying, security, and system operations on AWS.
For the Vietnam IT Job Market project, my next goal is to test each improvement, document actual results, and update technical instructions so that readers can reproduce the workflow more easily.

title: Feedback
content:
This section presents my personal reflections and suggestions — Vu Thi Phuc, a student of class K68CNTTB at the Vietnam National University of Agriculture — after participating in the First Cloud AI Journey program and working on the Vietnam IT Job Market project. As a student gradually exploring the field of technology, I aim to gain practical knowledge, improve my technical skills, and build a solid foundation for my future career in data engineering and cloud computing.
Evaluation by Category 1. Learning Environment
I find the learning approach, which combines documentation with hands-on exercises on Cloud Journey, suitable for my learning needs. Exploring individual AWS services and relating them to the project helps me better understand how theoretical knowledge can be applied in practice. I have also realized the importance of proactively reviewing lab instructions, preparing the necessary requirements, and checking configurations to ensure a smoother learning experience.
2. Learning Materials and Support
The learning materials are organized into specific topics, making it easier for me to follow the lessons and review information when necessary. During the learning process, whenever I encounter difficulties, I have gradually developed the habit of investigating possible causes, reviewing the steps I have taken, and recording error messages before seeking assistance. I have also become more aware of the importance of protecting personal and sensitive information when discussing technical issues.
3. Relevance to Information Technology
The learning content is closely related to several areas of Information Technology, including programming, databases, computer networks, and data storage technologies. Through the Vietnam IT Job Market project, I have explored the process of collecting recruitment data from ITviec using Python on EC2, processing JSON data, converting it into Parquet format, and storing it in Amazon S3. The data is then managed through AWS Glue Data Catalog, queried using Amazon Athena, and displayed on a Streamlit dashboard. This experience has given me a clearer understanding of how different components are developed and connected within a data processing system.
4. Most Improved Skills
Improved my ability to independently study documentation and understand the functions of different AWS services. Learned how to check IAM permissions, service configurations, storage paths, and logs when troubleshooting issues. Gained a better understanding of data storage, processing, and management in cloud computing environments. Developed the habit of recording commands, practical results, and errors for future reference and verification. Improved my ability to summarize and present knowledge through learning journals, reports, and workshops. 5. Community Culture
I appreciate the spirit of mutual support, knowledge sharing, and collaborative learning within the AWS Study Group community. For students who are new to AWS, referring to documentation and exchanging experiences with more knowledgeable members can make the learning process more effective. I hope to continue learning from the community, participating in its activities, and sharing the practical knowledge I have gained.
6. Practical Learning Conditions
Through AWS hands-on exercises, I have learned that cloud resources must be managed carefully because configuration changes can affect system operations, access permissions, and costs. Therefore, before starting a lab, it is important to define clear objectives, check available resources, and understand how to evaluate the results. After completing the exercises, reviewing and cleaning up unnecessary resources is also an essential practice.
Feedback Questions What Did You Like Most?
What I appreciate most is the opportunity to connect the knowledge I have learned with a practical project such as Vietnam IT Job Market. Exploring the process of storing Parquet data in S3, managing metadata with Glue, querying data through Athena, and visualizing results using Streamlit has helped me better understand the role of each technology. In addition, I have developed the ability to verify results and evaluate the functions implemented during system development.
What Could Be Improved in the Program?
Provide preparation guidelines before each learning module, including prerequisite knowledge, access permissions, and required resources. Include more examples of common errors related to IAM, Security Groups, Regions, and S3 paths, along with instructions for identifying their causes. Introduce short self-assessment exercises to help learners evaluate their understanding before moving on to the next topic. Encourage students to maintain regular worklogs, recording their results and experiences throughout the hands-on learning process. Would You Recommend This Program to Your Friends?
Yes. I would recommend this program to students who are interested in learning about AWS and cloud computing. In my opinion, the program provides opportunities to gain knowledge through hands-on practice while developing independent research and problem-solving skills. However, to achieve good results, participants should actively study the documentation, complete lab exercises, and take notes on important concepts.
Additional Suggestions Cost and Resource Management Guidance: Provide additional information about services that may incur costs, how to monitor resource usage, and how to clean up resources after completing lab exercises. More Group Discussion Activities: Encourage students to present different parts of their projects, such as data collection, processing, querying, and dashboard development, so they can exchange knowledge and receive constructive feedback. Additional Troubleshooting Exercises: Introduce practical scenarios involving log analysis, pipeline error identification, data verification, and recovery methods in testing environments. Standardized Practice Result Documentation: Provide guidance on recording execution times, commands, source code versions, and query results to make verification and evaluation easier. Would You Like to Stay Involved in the Program?
Yes. I would like to continue expanding my AWS knowledge, participating in knowledge-sharing activities, and improving my skills in Python, Data Engineering, and Cloud Computing. Regarding the Vietnam IT Job Market project, I hope to further explore testing methods, improve query performance, and enhance my understanding of operating data systems in real-world environments.
Acknowledgements
I would like to express my sincere gratitude to the First Cloud AI Journey program, the mentors, and the AWS Study Group community for providing a valuable learning environment and useful educational resources. Participating in the program has helped me broaden my knowledge, recognize areas
